sources.reference: QS An-Nisa 4:11
sources.note: Children shares (son:daughter 2:1; a single daughter 1/2; two or more daughters 2/3) and each parent 1/6 when the deceased has a child; mother 1/3 when no child and no multiple siblings.

sources.reference: QS An-Nisa 4:12
sources.note: Spouse shares (husband 1/2 without child, 1/4 with child; wife 1/4 without child, 1/8 with child) and maternal (uterine) siblings — one gets 1/6, two or more share 1/3 collectively.

sources.reference: QS An-Nisa 4:176
sources.note: Kalalah: full/paternal sister 1/2 (single) or 2/3 (two or more); a brother takes the residue in the 2:1 male:female ratio with sisters.

sources.reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 6732 / Sahih Muslim 1615, narrated Ibn 'Abbas
sources.note: "Give the fixed shares (fara'id) to those entitled to them; whatever remains goes to the nearest male ('asabah)." Basis of the residuary rule.

sources.reference: Sunan Abi Dawud 2894 / Sunan al-Tirmidhi 2101, narrated al-Mughirah ibn Shu'bah
sources.note: The grandmother is assigned one sixth (1/6).

sources.reference: Athar of the Sahabah on al-jadd (grandfather); Fiqh al-Mawarith consensus
sources.note: In the absence of the father, the paternal grandfather substitutes for him (1/6 with a descendant, otherwise residuary), per the majority position adopted by KHI and classical Syafi'i for the common cases modeled here.

sources.reference: KHI Pasal 171
sources.note: Definitions: pewaris, ahli waris, harta warisan, harta bersama.

sources.reference: KHI Pasal 174
sources.note: Enumeration of heirs by blood (nasab) and by marriage.

sources.reference: KHI Pasal 175
sources.note: Ordering of obligations on the estate: funeral costs, then debts, then wasiat (max 1/3), then division among heirs.

sources.reference: KHI Pasal 176
sources.note: Daughter: 1/2 if sole; 2/3 if two or more; with a son the ratio is 2:1 male:female (asabah bi ghairihi).

sources.reference: KHI Pasal 177 (as interpreted per Mahkamah Agung jurisprudence)
sources.note: Literal text assigns the father 1/3 when there is no child, which conflicts with the fara'id system; Mahkamah Agung jurisprudence and mainstream KHI practice read the father as 1/6 when a descendant exists and residuary ('asabah) otherwise — the interpretation applied by this engine. UI must surface this caveat in Professional mode.

sources.reference: KHI Pasal 178
sources.note: Mother: 1/6 if there is a child or two or more siblings; otherwise 1/3.

sources.reference: KHI Pasal 179
sources.note: Widower (duda): 1/2 without child, 1/4 with child.

sources.reference: KHI Pasal 180
sources.note: Widow (janda): 1/4 without child, 1/8 with child.

sources.reference: KHI Pasal 181
sources.note: Maternal (uterine) siblings: one gets 1/6, two or more share 1/3 collectively; blocked by a child or the father.

sources.reference: KHI Pasal 182
sources.note: Full/paternal sister: 1/2 if sole, 2/3 if two or more; with a full/paternal brother the 2:1 ratio applies. Blocked by descendants and the father.

sources.reference: KHI Pasal 185
sources.note: Ahli waris pengganti (representation): children of an heir who predeceased the deceased may step into that heir's position, capped at the share the replaced heir would have received. NO classical Syafi'i equivalent (PRD §4.1).

sources.reference: KHI Pasal 192
sources.note: 'Aul: when fixed shares exceed the estate, shares are reduced proportionally.

sources.reference: KHI Pasal 193
sources.note: Radd: when fixed shares total less than the estate and no residuary heir exists, the surplus is returned proportionally to the fixed-share heirs.

sources.reference: KHI Pasal 209
sources.note: Wasiat wajibah: an obligatory bequest of at most 1/3 between an adopted child and their adoptive parents, who do not inherit from one another under faraid. NOT implemented — see faraid_engine.coverage.

sources.reference: Fiqh al-Mawarith (science of inheritance shares), general treatment

sources.note: Cross-reference for rule content and madhab divergence; text not reproduced.

sources.note: Proportional reduction of shares when the pokok masalah is over-subscribed. Valid bases: 6→7/8/9/10, 12→13/15/17, 24→27.

sources.reference: Radd doctrine — classical position; spouse excluded from radd (majority Sunni)
sources.note: In classical Syafi'i, when no ashabul furud remain to absorb the surplus and no asabah exist, the surplus historically routes to baitul mal rather than to the spouse. Rule-set dependent (PRD §5.2 step 7).

sources.reference: Dzawil arham routing — az-Zuhaili, comparative madhab treatment
sources.note: Reached only when no ashabul furud/asabah exist. Syafi'i/Maliki classically route to baitul mal; Hanafi/Hanbali distribute to dzawil arham (PRD §4.1).

sources.reference: Pengadilan Agama practice commentary on radd/dzawil arham vs. baitul mal
sources.note: In current Indonesian practice a functioning baitul mal claim mechanism does not exist, so PA generally applies radd to fixed-share heirs (including the spouse where no other heir remains) rather than escheating to baitul mal. sources.reference: Radd accepted (Hanafi & Hanbali) — surplus returned to non-spouse ashabul furud
sources.note: Spouse excluded from radd in the majority view.

sources.reference: Maliki: no radd — surplus escheats to baitul mal, which is treated as an heir
sources.note: The Maliki school does not apply radd; when fixed shares are under-subscribed and no asabah exist, the remainder goes to baitul mal.

sources.reference: KHI Pasal 96–97 (harta bersama) applied before faraid
sources.note: The surviving spouse's community-property share (typically 1/2 of joint assets) is separated BEFORE faraid applies to the remainder. An Indonesian civil-law concept with no classical-fiqh equivalent; off by default in classical Syafi'i mode (PRD §4.1).

sources.reference: Consensus on netting the estate (funeral, debts, wasiat) before faraid
